title: What's the Typical Architect Project Timeline in Westchester?
excerpt: Planning a home renovation or addition in Westchester? Here's what to expect from design through completion when you work with a licensed architect and general contractor under one roof.
content:
When homeowners in Scarsdale, Mamaroneck, or anywhere else across Westchester start thinking about a renovation or addition, one question comes up fast: how long is this going to take? It's a fair question. Your home is your biggest investment, and you want to know what the timeline looks like before you commit.

The truth is, there's no single answer that fits every project. A kitchen remodel moves differently than a second-story addition. A historic restoration in Tarrytown has different demands than a new primary suite in Rye. But there are real stages every project goes through, and understanding them helps you plan better.

The Design Phase Usually Takes 4 to 8 Weeks

This is where it all starts. You meet with an architect to talk through what you want. You share ideas, photos, and your budget. A licensed architect in Westchester, NY will walk through your home, measure spaces, take notes, and understand how your project fits into the existing structure.

Then comes the drawing work. Your architect develops sketches, floor plans, and elevations that show what the finished space will look like. You review, give feedback, and refinements happen. This back-and-forth is normal and necessary. It's the time to get it right on paper before anyone swings a hammer.

Once the design is locked in, your architect prepares construction documents. These are the detailed plans and specifications that contractors bid from and build to. In municipalities like White Plains, Bronxville, and Harrison, these documents also become the basis for permit applications.

Permitting Takes Longer Than Most People Expect

Every town in Westchester has its own building department and permit process. Pelham Manor has one. Eastchester has another. Hastings-on-Hudson has its own. This isn't a problem specific to one town. It's just how it works across the county.

Permitting typically takes 4 to 12 weeks, depending on the scope of work and the municipality. A kitchen renovation might move faster than a home addition in Ossining that requires zoning review. A general contractor in Westchester who also holds an architect's license, like Silvio M. Luca at House Architecture & Construction, knows how each town's planning process works. He runs every project personally, which means no surprises about how long approvals will take.

Some projects need multiple permits or board approvals. An open-concept conversion might trigger structural review. A new construction or major renovation in Dobbs Ferry might need site plan approval. Your architect and contractor should tell you upfront what to expect.

Construction Duration Depends on Scope

This is where project size really matters. A bathroom renovation might take 4 to 6 weeks. A kitchen remodel could run 8 to 12 weeks. A second-story addition or primary suite addition takes longer, usually 12 to 20 weeks or more once work starts.

New custom construction in Westchester County takes the longest, often 6 months to over a year depending on complexity. Historic restorations in towns like Tuckahoe or Larchmont sometimes run longer because you're working around existing conditions and period details that demand care.

When you hire a design-build firm in Westchester, you eliminate coordination delays between separate architects and contractors. Silvio works as both, which means decisions move faster and the budget stays cleaner.

Start to Finish

Add it all up. Design takes 4 to 8 weeks. Permits take 4 to 12 weeks. Construction takes anywhere from 4 weeks to over a year. A typical home renovation or addition from first meeting to final walkthrough runs 6 to 9 months for smaller projects, and longer for larger ones.
